Lunch note, Butterfly Room. Aparna.
Noor pushed away the beans again today, the fifth day in a row. She pinched one, said "squishy", and stuck out her tongue. Last month I tried coaxing, "One bite and you get a sticker", and she cried and ate nothing. So now I just put a few beans on her plate, say nothing, and eat mine next to her. Today she licked one. Tomorrow I'll do the same.

qa.a: Noor said "squishy".

qa.q: Why might Noor have stuck out her tongue at the bean?
qa.a: Noor seemed to dislike the squishy texture and felt put off by it.

qa.q: What went wrong last month, and what works better now?
qa.a: Bribing with a sticker made Noor cry and eat nothing; calmly offering a few beans with no fuss led to a first lick.

qa.q: How might Aparna feel seeing Noor lick a bean?
qa.a: Aparna would likely feel quietly encouraged, seeing that patience is working.

grounding: A young child refuses a food because of its texture, and calm repeated offering without bribes slowly widens her taste.

In their village near Bareilly, five-year-old Hafsa folded her arms at the sight of karela on her plate. "No. It's yucky." Dadi leaned in. "Eat it or no sweet tonight!" Hafsa's lip shook, and she shoved the plate away so hard the roti slid off.
The next day, Hafsa's mother, Reena, tried something else. She put a tiny piece of karela beside Hafsa's rice and said nothing. Hafsa ignored it. Reena ate hers calmly. On the fourth day, Hafsa poked it. On the seventh, she nibbled a corner, made a face and said, "Still yucky. But a little bit okay."

qa.q: Which vegetable did Hafsa refuse?
qa.a: Hafsa refused karela.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel when Dadi threatened no sweet?
qa.a: Hafsa felt upset and pushed; her lip shook and she shoved the plate away.

qa.q: Why did Reena's approach work better than Dadi's?
qa.a: Reena offered a tiny piece calmly each day without pressure, so Hafsa could come to it herself instead of fighting.

qa.q: How might Dadi see Reena's quiet approach?
qa.a: Dadi might think it too soft at first, since she believes in rules like "eat it or no sweet".

grounding: A young child refuses food and resists pressure, and calm repeated offering without fuss slowly widens her taste.

'Mehak, eat your dal. One more spoon and you get a chocolate.'
'NO! It's yucky!'
Sangeeta sighed. Every night was the same. Then she remembered what the doctor at the check-up had said. She put the spoon down. 'Okay. You don't have to eat it.'
Mehak looked suspicious. 'No chocolate?'
'No chocolate, no fighting. The dal is just there if you want it.'
Sangeeta ate her own dal and talked about the pigeon on the balcony.
Mehak watched. After a while, she dipped her roti in the dal. Just the edge.
'Hmm,' she said.
Sangeeta didn't cheer. She just kept talking about the pigeon.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta offer Mehak at first for eating dal?
qa.a: A chocolate.

qa.q: How did Mehak feel when the bribes stopped?
qa.a: She was suspicious and curious, not sure what was happening.

qa.q: Why did Sangeeta not cheer when Mehak dipped her roti?
qa.a: Making a fuss could have turned eating back into a contest; staying calm let Mehak try it on her own terms.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta feel as Mehak dips her roti?
qa.a: She is probably pleased and hopeful, but careful not to show it too much so the calm continues.

grounding: Shows a young child refusing food and a parent dropping bribes and pressure for calm offering, which lets the child try on her own.

Note from the preschool kitchen, Friday
For his first month here, Ojas ate only plain rice. Every day he pushed the vegetables away and cried if anyone coaxed him. We tried stickers; it made things worse. So we stopped. Now we put a small spoon of vegetables beside his rice each day and don't mention it. He sits with children who enjoy their food. On Monday he touched a carrot. Wednesday he sniffed it. Today he ate two pieces, then went back to rice. No one clapped. We'll keep offering, calmly. Please do the same at home; no pressure needed.
Sangeeta, kitchen staff

qa.a: Calmly offering a small spoon of vegetables daily without mentioning it.

qa.a: They would likely feel hopeful and reassured that calm offering is working.

grounding: Shows a young child refusing many foods, and how dropping rewards and pressure for calm repeated offering slowly widens his taste.
